what: The idea: scale x dependence x assumptions
title: Choosing the right test (and mixed models)
text: principled model choice product three questions, order: outcome’s measurement scale? fixes model family (Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, cumulative-link) anything else. observations independent clustered? Repeated measures grouped structure needs random effects, .e. mixed model. continuous outcome, parametric assumptions hold? Group-wise normality (, subjects, homogeneity variance) decides parametric rank-based method. classify_outcome() answers first question. maps variable one "continuous", "ordinal", "binary", "count", "nominal" using simple, transparent rules (ordered factor -> ordinal; two distinct values -> binary; -valued integer -> ordinal/Likert; non-negative integer values -> count; anything else numeric -> continuous). Getting scale right matters , analyst’s habit, dictates family: 1-5 rating interval score, 0/1 accuracy Gaussian. heuristic genuinely ambiguous (wide Likert item versus small count) can override via outcome_type argument recommend_test().
code: set.seed(1) n_id <- 24 d <- data.frame(   id   = factor(rep(seq_len(n_id), each = 3)),   cond = factor(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), times = n_id)) )  # Give condition a genuine effect so the example models are well identified. step <- c(A = 0, B = 1.3, C = 2.4)[as.character(d$cond)] d$score   <- as.numeric(step + rnorm(nrow(d))) d$rating  <- ordered(pmin(5L, pmax(1L, round(step + rnorm(nrow(d), sd = 0.7) + 2)))) d$correct <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(step - 1))  classify_outcome(d$score)    # continuous #> [1] "continuous" classify_outcome(d$rating)   # ordinal (ordered factor) #> [1] "ordinal" classify_outcome(d$correct)  # binary (two distinct values) #> [1] "binary"

cond + (1 | id), data = your_data)  # outcome must be an ordered factor #>   Report with    : reportCLMM() #>   Alternative(s) : nparLD (rank-based repeated measures) if proportional odds is untenable Design         : between #>   Normality      : not rejected #>   Homogeneity    : not rejected #>   Recommendation : One-way ANOVA (parametric) #>   Family         : gaussian #>   Fit with       : ggbetweenstatsWithPriorNormalityCheck(data = your_data, x = "cond", y = "score") #>   Report with    : reportggstatsplot() #>   Alternative(s) : none needed #>   Rationale      : the outcome is continuous and normally distributed with homogeneous variances, so a parametric ANOVA is appropriate rec_clmm$model_function #> [1] "ordinal::clmm" rec_clmm$reporter #> [1] "reportCLMM" observations are clustered within `id` (24 clusters, 72 observations). A Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM), binomial (`lme4::glmer`) is therefore recommended; report it with `reportGLMM()`.

what: Fitting and reporting the recommended models
title: Choosing the right test (and mixed models)
text: model fitted, reporters turn manuscript-ready LaTeX/APA sentences, one per fixed-effect term, effect size, confidence interval, test statistic, p-value. reportGLMM() handles lme4::lmer / lme4::glmer / glmmTMB::glmmTMB plain lm/glm; reportCLMM() handles ordinal::clmm / ordinal::clm. reporters pick effect-size scale family: odds ratios binomial cumulative-link models, incidence-rate ratios counts, raw coefficients (b) t/z statistic Gaussian fits. fits require lme4, ordinal, parameters (Suggests), chunk guarded has_mixed; vignette still builds without . ordinal recommendation, fit CLMM report reportCLMM(). family cumulative-link, effects reported odds ratios (multiplicative change odds higher rating): binary recommendation, fit binomial GLMM report reportGLMM(); binomial family likewise exponentiated odds ratios, z statistic: reportGLMM() also covers Gaussian mixed ordinary models. linear mixed model reported raw coefficient scale, b t(df) statistic rather odds ratio – reporter adapts wording family automatically: reporters return sentences invisibly (emit via message()), can optionally copy clipboard (write_to_clipboard = TRUE) write .tex file \input{} manuscript (sink_to =). LaTeX uses \p / \pminor macros latex_preamble().
code: m_clmm <- ordinal::clmm(rating ~ cond + (1 | id), data = d) reportCLMM(m_clmm, dv = "rating") #> A cumulative link mixed model was fitted for rating. #> The effect of \textit{condB} on rating was significant ($OR = 309.89$, 95\% CI $[26.21, 3663.95]$, $z = 4.55$, \pminor{0.001}). #> The effect of \textit{condC} on rating was significant ($OR = 10085.81$, 95\% CI $[384.38, 264641.13]$, $z = 5.53$, \pminor{0.001}). m_glmm <- lme4::glmer(correct ~ cond + (1 | id), data = d, family = binomial) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') reportGLMM(m_glmm, dv = "accuracy") #> A generalized linear mixed model was fitted for accuracy. #> The effect of \textit{condB} on accuracy was not significant ($OR = 2.80$, 95\% CI $[0.87, 9.06]$, $z = 1.72$, \p{0.086}). #> The effect of \textit{condC} on accuracy was significant ($OR = 7.60$, 95\% CI $[2.07, 27.89]$, $z = 3.06$, \p{0.002}). m_lmm <- lme4::lmer(score ~ cond + (1 | id), data = d) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') reportGLMM(m_lmm, dv = "score") #> A linear mixed model was fitted for score. #> The effect of \textit{condB} on score was significant ($b = 1.28$, 95\% CI $[0.74, 1.81]$, $t(67) = 4.77$, \pminor{0.001}). #> The effect of \textit{condC} on score was significant ($b = 2.20$, 95\% CI $[1.67, 2.73]$, $t(67) = 8.21$, \pminor{0.001}).

text: analyze_and_report(): one-call pipeline per dependent variable – assumption checks ready-made methods sentence, matching ggstatsplot figure (automatic parametric/non-parametric selection), omnibus result, post-hoc comparisons. report_all(): runs analyze_and_report() many dependent variables (e.g., questionnaire scales study), returns summary table Holm-adjusted omnibus p-values across DVs, combined figure patchwork installed. latex_preamble(): prints (writes file) complete set LaTeX \newcommand definitions required report functions – hunting individual help pages. report functions accept sink_to write output .tex file, manuscripts can \input{} results stay date analysis re-run. also invisibly return text programmatic use (e.g., inline Quarto/R Markdown). save_paper_figure(): saves plots publication presets (ACM-style single-column 3.33 / full-width 7 ). PDFs use Cairo embedded fonts Windows/Linux; macOS default pdf device used R’s cairo can crash session (observed segfaults GitHub Actions macOS runners). device argument allows overriding. assumption_methods_text(): turns Shapiro-Wilk (optionally Levene) checks methods-section justification sentence reviewers expect, including test statistics. check_normality_by_group() check_homogeneity_by_group() now attach test statistics attributes. cite_methods(): prints methods boilerplate plus BibTeX entries packages behind analyses (ART, Dunn, nparLD, ggstatsplot, effectsize). Consistent snake_case aliases discoverable prefixes whole API (e.g., report_art(), report_dunn_test(), plot_between_stats(), check_assumptions_anova()). original names remain fully supported. New option options(colleyRstats.leading_zero = FALSE) APA-style p-values effect sizes without leading zero (e.g., p=.033). Significance brackets asterisk plot helpers now stacked relative data range, layout works dependent-variable scale (1-7 Likert 0-100 TLX alike).

title: colleyRstats 0.1.0
text: reportggstatsplot() now recognizes unpaired non-parametric test (“Wilcoxon rank sum test”, reported W statistic); previously results fell generic fallback format. signed-rank (paired) variant keeps V statistic. p-value also compared rounding, e.g. p = 0.0009 reported “p < 0.001” . reportNPAV(), reportART(), reportNparLD() write_to_clipboard = TRUE now write significant effects clipboard ; previously effect overwrote previous one last sentence survived. functions now also invisibly return reported sentences. asterisk plot helpers (ggbetweenstatsWithPriorNormalityCheckAsterisk(), ggwithinstatsWithPriorNormalityCheckAsterisk()) longer drop significant comparisons whose adjusted p-value exactly 0.01 0.001. replace_values() longer round-trips untouched numeric columns .character(), silently truncated values 15 significant digits. reportggstatsplotPostHoc() handles missing values dependent variable (na.rm = TRUE) falls back raw level name label_mappings entry missing instead producing malformed text. reportNparLD() output now correctly says “nparLD analysis” instead “NPAV”, required \df LaTeX command documented. reportDunnTestTable() reportArtConTable(): orderByP = TRUE now takes precedence default alphabetical ordering instead silently undone . Partial eta squared reportART()/reportNPAV() now computed unrounded F statistic. rFromWilcoxAdjusted() caps adjusted p-value 1, avoiding NaN results. generateMoboPlot2() stops clear error phase column lacks “sampling”/“optimization” rows instead producing -Inf positions. normalize() rejects zero-width input range instead returning Inf/NaN. remove_outliers_REI() now actually uses range argument (validation plus --range warning) ignores NA responses tallying instead poisoning row counts. reshape_data() reports clear error marker-delimited sections unequal column counts. checkAssumptionsForAnova() distinguishes “normality assessed” “normality violated” uses consistent p < 0.05 boundary. Effect-size failures Dunn/ART post-hoc reporters now emit warning instead silently swallowed. four gg*WithPriorNormalityCheck*() wrappers now pass palette "pals::glasbey" format required current ggstatsplot; deprecated package=/palette= pair ignored warning, plots silently used default palette instead glasbey.
